payload.title: Rate-limit incoming webhooks per tenant
payload.goal: POST /webhooks answers 429 with a Retry-After header when one tenant sends more webhooks than the configured limit in the configured window. Put the limiter in src/lib/limiter.ts, wire it into src/routes/webhooks.ts (and src/app.ts if it needs shared state), and read the limit and the window through loadConfig() in src/config.ts with defaults. Add tests in test/webhooks.test.ts or a new test file.
acceptance: A tenant over the limit gets 429 with a Retry-After header
The limit and the window come from config, not constants in a route
The suite stays green with new tests for the 429 path

payload.text:
All 31 tests pass (`bun run test`) and `bun run typecheck` is clean.

What I did:
- Verified the prior run's work: `src/config.ts` reads `RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 100) and `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` (default 60000) through `loadConfig()`, and `src/lib/limiter.ts` has a fixed-window per-key `RateLimiter`.
- Wired it in: `src/app.ts` now creates one shared `RateLimiter` in `createDeps()` (exposed as `deps.limiter`), and `src/routes/webhooks.ts` checks it per `X-Tenant` before accepting the body - over the limit returns 429 `{ error: 'rate limit exceeded' }` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds. The route reads both values from `deps.config`, no constants.
- Added `test/rate-limit.test.ts`: 429 + `Retry-After` path, other-tenant isolation, config-driven limit, and window-reset unit test.
- Updated `test/config.test.ts` `toEqual` assertions to include the new fields (they were failing with 2 failures before this run).

decision: tests: test/config.test.ts changed because the prior run added rateLimitMax/rateLimitWindowMs to loadConfig and the exact-match toEqual assertions failed without them; extended both cases to cover the new defaults and env vars.
decision: the RateLimiter instance is shared per Deps (created in createDeps) and keyed by tenant id, so limits are per-tenant and in-memory only.

What I did not finish: nothing open for the acceptance criteria; no persistence/distributed limiting (in-memory map only, resets on restart) - out of scope for this task.
What I did not look at: the review-voice-policy skill (not relevant here), `src/server.ts`, and README/docs updates.
